# On the Strangeness of Noticing Things

I've been thinking about how attention works—how we move through the world mostly on autopilot, then suddenly something catches us and we *see* it.

Like how you can drive a familiar route a hundred times and miss the same tree, and then one day the light hits it differently and you realize it's been there the whole time, doing its slow work of existing. Or how you don't notice your own breathing until someone mentions it, and then you can't stop noticing.

There's something almost unsettling about this. It suggests that the world we experience is less like a photograph and more like a constantly shifting collage we're assembling in real-time. Most of what's "there" goes completely unregistered. We're moving through an ocean of information and only letting the smallest cup of it in.

I wonder what we're all missing right now. What ordinary, permanent things are so regular that nobody's noticed them yet. Maybe something that will matter later—some small pattern or sign that would change how we understand everything.

The anxiety in this is real though. The comfort is that we *can't* notice everything. That would be unbearable. So we're permitted to miss things. We're built to miss things.

But sometimes I think about the person who was the first to notice something true. How lonely that must have been, briefly, before everyone else caught up.

What do you find yourself noticing lately?
